definitions.gloss: to take out, to bring out
definitions.explanation: To remove something from inside a container or place and bring it outside or into view.
To formally present documents, homework, or applications to someone in authority.

examples.japanese: かばんから{本|ほん}を{出|だ}してください。
examples.english: Please take the book out of the bag.

examples.japanese: {宿題|しゅくだい}を{出|だ}しましたか。
examples.english: Did you hand in your homework?

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}に{手紙|てがみ}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I sent a letter to my friend.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pair: {出|で}る (intransitive). Pattern: Xを{出|だ}す (take out X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing action or result. {出|だ}している = 'is putting out' or 'has taken out.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{手紙|てがみ}を{出|だ}す (send a letter)
・{宿題|しゅくだい}を{出|だ}す (submit homework)
・ゴミを{出|だ}す (put out trash)
・{声|こえ}を{出|だ}す (speak up/make a sound)

AUXILIARY: V-stem + {出|だ}す = start doing suddenly: {走|はし}り{出|だ}す (start running), {泣|な}き{出|だ}す (burst into tears).

PAIR: {出|で}る (intransitive) - {結果|けっか}が{出|で}た (results came out).
